chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Clarence Profit at the Rhythm Club
summary: Everyone including the Lion and Jelly Roll stopped to hear the crippled West Indian Profit play at the Rhythm Club.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, Clarence Profit... When they used to have the sessions, Clarence Profit would come around the Rhythm Club, and they asked him, "Play something, Clarence." When Clarence played, everybody listened, the Lion and Jelly Roll -- everybody listened at this little crippled boy. He had a funny foot, he was sick. And he was from the West Indies Islands, he was a West Indian. And his father was a neat West Indian man who played piano, and he would come and play something around -- nobody paid him no mind. And they'd say, "That's Clarence Profit's father." He'd get at the piano and play, just playin', just the ordinary piano, you know. But he loved to hear 'em talk about "That's Clarence Profit's father." Then you'd see Clarence Profit comin', and everybody put their pool sticks down and everything, and listen to Clarence Profit.
